brief.topic: Your agent demo succeeded 9 times. Why it still fails in production
brief.audience: PMs and engineers building multi-step agents
constraints: Illustrative numbers labelled on screen and in caption

coreInsight: Per-step reliability multiplies across long tasks, so evaluate end-to-end task success over many runs instead of trusting a few successful demos.

hooks.notes: Specific and surprising; the reel shows the arithmetic.

hooks.text: Agents don’t fail at a step. They fail at the sum.
hooks.notes: Elegant but abstract for two seconds.

hooks.text: The math that breaks long agent tasks.

caption.opening: A step that works 95% of the time sounds solid. Chain ten of them and it’s closer to a coin flip with good odds.
body: Illustrative math (assuming independent steps): 0.95 × 0.95 … ten times ≈ 0.60. Real systems differ, but the direction holds: long tasks amplify small error rates.

So evaluate the whole task, many times:
→ end-to-end success rate over dozens of runs
→ where in the chain failures cluster
→ which steps need a check or a human approval
(Numbers in the reel are illustrative, not measurements of a real system.)

claims.text: 95% per-step success over 10 independent steps ≈ 60% end-to-end (0.95^10 ≈ 0.599).
Agent reliability should be evaluated end to end over many runs rather than inferred from successful demos.
